findings.title: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')
findings.trigger: If 'n', 'm', 'k', or 'h' contain special characters or are crafted in a way to manipulate the program flow, it could lead to unintended behavior.
findings.assumptions: The 'read' macro uses 'cin' to read variables 'n', 'm', 'k', and 'h'. The values of these variables are then used in subsequent calculations and conditions.

findings.title: Buffer Over-read
findings.trigger: If 'n' is greater than the actual size of the vector 'v', it could lead to a buffer over-read.
findings.assumptions: The vector 'v' is initialized with size 'n' on line 26. The loop on line 27 reads 'n' elements into 'v'. If 'n' is not properly validated, it could cause a buffer over-read.

findings.title: Stack-based Buffer Overflow
findings.trigger: If 'n' is significantly large, it could cause a stack overflow due to excessive memory allocation for the vector 'v'.
findings.assumptions: The vector 'v' is allocated on the stack. If 'n' is not properly constrained, it could lead to a stack overflow.

findings.title: Division or Modulo by Zero
findings.trigger: If 'k' is zero, it will cause a division by zero error.
findings.assumptions: The value of 'k' is read from the user on line 24. If 'k' is zero, the modulo operation on line 36 will result in a division by zero.
